reason: REFUTED on the citation standard, not on the attribution. The attribution, play, act, scene and speaker are almost certainly right: Emily asks it of the Stage Manager in the Act III graveyard scene after reliving her twelfth birthday, and he answers No, the saints and poets, maybe. But the card's whole claim to ship rests on one assertion the evidence could not support and that I found to be contested. The evidence says the printed sentence continues past the question mark and so the card stops at a question mark the edition itself prints. No edition was opened, by the verifier's own admission, and the cited URL is LitCharts, a study guide. I reached four further independent renderings and they do not agree on the punctuation the card depends on. StageAgent's monologue text, oldfirstucc.org and quotes.net print Do any human beings ever realize life while they live it? dash every, every minute? with the question mark after it. Another rendering surfaced in search prints Do any human beings ever realize life while they live it dash every, every minute? with NO question mark after it, the dash running straight on. A third widely circulated rendering, on Goodreads under an EMILY: speech prefix, reads Does anyone ever realize life while they live it, which is a different sentence altogether. If the second rendering is the printed one, the card's terminal question mark is minted punctuation and rule 6 is broken; if the third is, the wording is wrong. Nothing in the evidence resolves this, and exactly this drift between renderings is the failure this track exists to catch. Second and independent ground: rule 12 requires that where the trail runs out the card HEDGE with a note that says so plainly, and the verifier's own verdict file records confidence medium because no edition was opened, yet the card's note field is empty. The uncertainty would ship invisibly, which is the March hedge's mistake repeated. Everything else checks out and should be preserved if the line is rescued: shipped.js returns nothing shipped, nothing near, Wilder at one for the year from the February Bridge of San Luis Rey line and so under the cap, not banned, not in personsUsed for June; in scope as a play first published 1938; no content warning needed; source line 82 characters, leads with the name, no em dash, no straight double quote, tag Drama is the form. Two smaller points for whoever rescues it: in Act III Emily is Emily Gibbs, married to George, and only Wilder's cast list still calls her Emily Webb, so the parenthesis should say (Emily) or (Emily Gibbs); and her question to the Stage Manager (Emily Webb) names the speaker twice over. REMEDY: open a printed copy, Coward-McCann 1938 or the HarperCollins Perennial Classics reissue, read the punctuation after it, and ship the sentence whole in the edition's own marks, naming that edition. Until then the line is not verified and must not ride the carry as though it were.
